note: Deterministic bootstrap for the Spring-compatibility path (SAD v3 §6). Every row is a documented Quarkus mapping, never an inference: starters map to the Quarkus Spring compatibility extensions and their runtime prerequisites; property keys map per the quarkus-spring-boot-properties and hibernate-orm guides. Versions are never here: the BOM and plugin come from .hermes/pins.json (quarkus_platform, compiler_plugin, surefire_plugin). A starter or driver without a row stays in the pom and is surfaced by the compiler and the MTA rescan as work-list items; nothing is guessed.

main_class.note: Quarkus has no application main class on the compat path; the file is deleted and recorded in the bootstrap receipt.

maven_settings.reason: Red Hat build of Quarkus artifacts (com.redhat.quarkus.platform:*-redhat-*) are published on the Red Hat GA repository, not Maven Central
maven_settings.source: https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_quarkus/3.27/html/getting_started_with_red_hat_build_of_quarkus/proc_configuring-maven-settings_quarkus-getting-started (Configuring the Maven settings.xml file for the online repository)

starter_notes.org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-sta: No Quarkus Spring-compatibility extension covers Spring AOP (the quarkus.io Spring guides list DI, Web, Data JPA, Security, Cache, Scheduled, Boot properties only). The starter is dropped; every @Aspect / org.aspectj use is either retired by an ADR (decisions.yaml retired_sources) or surfaced by the compiler as a work-list item for a CDI-interceptor rewrite. Nothing is guessed.

logging.level..source: https://quarkus.io/guides/logging#logging-categories (MTA rule springboot-properties-to-quarkus-00003 links the same guide)

artifact_aliases.note: Artifacts that MTA's Quarkus 2-era advice names by their pre-3.9 id. The pinned BOM manages only the renamed id (Quarkus 3.9 migration guide, 'RESTEasy Reactive renamed to Quarkus REST'); the brief points the worker at the managed name so it never adds an unversioned, unmanaged dependency.

package_renames.note: Jakarta EE 10 namespace (Quarkus 3 migration guide, 'Jakarta EE 10' section): javax.* → jakarta.* for these packages. The brief attaches the rename to a compiler diagnostic that names one of them; the worker changes the import, never the dependency.

plugin_config.note: Documented configuration of build plugins that generate sources, applied by the bootstrap when the plugin is present. Each row: the version (a measured Maven Central release), configuration leaves set wherever they appear under the plugin, and configOptions entries. openapi-generator: the `spring` generator (library spring-boot) emits javax.validation and springfox annotations; the documented Quarkus target is generator `jaxrs-spec` with library `quarkus` and useJakartaEe (openapi-generator generator reference for jaxrs-spec).

org.openapitools:openapi-generator-maven.note_source_folder: jaxrs-spec writes to <output>/src/gen/java by default while the plugin registers <output>/<configOptions.sourceFolder or src/main/java> as a compile source root (CodeGenMojo.getCompileSourceRoot, 7.25.0). Pinning sourceFolder makes the two agree and matches the source root the legacy build-helper already registers. Measured live 2026-09-10 on pilot v7: without it Maven failed at default-compile on missing DTOs while the generated files sat in src/gen/java.

org.jacoco:jacoco-maven-plugin.note: JaCoCo before 0.8.11 cannot read Java 21 class files (major version 65) and fails the report goal with UnsupportedClassVersionError; 0.8.11 is the release that officially supports Java 21 (https://github.com/jacoco/jacoco/releases/tag/v0.8.11). The pinned structure_extractor toolchain is jdk-21, so a legacy pom carrying 0.8.7 breaks mvn package on the destination. Measured live 2026-09-10 on pilot v7: the loop never saw it because the measure stops at the test phase.

remove_dependencies.note: Legacy dependencies with a documented replacement (or none) on this platform; the bootstrap removes them and adds the replacement extensions. Rows measured on pilot v6 (2026-09-10): the loop accepted each of these pom edits one card at a time.

org.springframework.data:spring-data-jdb.source: https://quarkus.io/guides/spring-data-jpa (Spring Data JDBC has no Quarkus compatibility extension; JDBC access on Quarkus is Agroal, quarkus-agroal comes with the JPA starter mapping)

replace_dependencies.note: javax → jakarta artifact renames the BOM manages (MTA javax-to-jakarta-dependencies-00001/00003).

plugins_to_add.note: Plugins the platform guide adds when absent (MTA javaee-pom-to-quarkus-00040; https://quarkus.io/guides/maven-tooling).

profile_files.note: Spring profile files application-<profile>.properties are merged into application.properties as %<profile>.<key> and removed (https://quarkus.io/guides/config-reference#profiles; MTA springboot-properties-to-quarkus-00001). Keys are mapped first (properties / property_prefixes).

test_scoped.note: Artifacts the mapping adds in test scope.

datasources.note: The destination platform's documented JDBC extensions, one row per quarkus.datasource.db-kind (RHBQ 3.27 Configure data sources: https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_quarkus/3.27/html/configure_data_sources/datasources). A db-kind with no row here is not configurable on this platform: hsqldb and derby-in-memory legacies therefore need an explicit engine decision (decisions.yaml datasource), never a silent driver swap.

postgresql.note: RHBQ 3.27 Configure data sources, PostgreSQL: quarkus-jdbc-postgresql.

mysql.note: RHBQ 3.27 Configure data sources, MySQL: quarkus-jdbc-mysql.

mariadb.note: RHBQ 3.27 Configure data sources, MariaDB: quarkus-jdbc-mariadb.

mssql.note: RHBQ 3.27 Configure data sources, Microsoft SQL Server: quarkus-jdbc-mssql.

db2.note: RHBQ 3.27 Configure data sources, IBM Db2: quarkus-jdbc-db2.

h2.note: RHBQ 3.27 Configure data sources, H2: quarkus-jdbc-h2. In-memory H2 is a development database, not a parity referent for a run that must prove persistence effects.

derby.note: RHBQ 3.27 Configure data sources, Apache Derby: quarkus-jdbc-derby.

oracle.note: RHBQ 3.27 Configure data sources, Oracle: quarkus-jdbc-oracle.

effective_keys.note: The unprefixed keys the destination must carry for the decided engine. A profile-prefixed key alone is not a configured datasource: Quarkus resolves db-kind at build time, and pilot v7 failed augmentation with 'Datasource <default> is not configured' while %hsqldb.* keys sat in application.properties.
